author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected forward. The correction form opens prefilled with the current values; a valid submission updates the same visit in place and shows the owner's record; the pet gains no second visit. Correction validates as booking does: description required, date in the future.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a booked visit's correction form shows it prefilled with the visit's current date and description
Submitting a description and a date later than today updates that same visit's date and description and shows the owner's record
A successful correction leaves the pet's visit count unchanged — no second visit is added
A blank description is refused and the description is named
A date of today or earlier is refused and the date is named
Correcting a visit that does not belong to the named pet, or a pet not belonging to the named owner, is refused
non_goals: Cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-5, NG-4)
A visible entry point to correction — no edit link is added to the owner detail page in this slice
notes: Narrows NG-5 per adr/2026-08-28-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowing.md. Open question recorded in PRD: whether the owner's record gains a visible way into correction later. docs/adr/README.md index needs a new row for the 2026-08-28 ADR — outside product-requirements-expert write scope (README is not a *-non-goal-*.md file); flagging for the ADR-index owner.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the existing edit-in-place pattern the sample already demonstrates for owners and pets (createOrUpdateOwnerForm / createOrUpdatePetForm: GET prefills the existing entity, POST validates and saves through the aggregate root). This slice extends that same forward-only correction to Visit, the leaf of the Owner->Pet->Visit aggregate, reusing OwnerRepository as the sole write path (system-design Overview, Contracts § invariants). No new module, pattern, or ADR — the product decision is already recorded in adr/2026-08-28-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowing.md (NG-5 narrowing). The one adjustment: adapt VisitController's shared @ModelAttribute to serve both the new-visit and edit-visit paths, and add aggregate navigation to reach an existing Visit. system-design.md is unchanged: the mental model is intact and the code does not exist yet, so the VisitController contract row is updated when the implementation lands, not at triage.
integration_points: GET+POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit added to VisitController, rendering the existing pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template
Update path saves through OwnerRepository.save(owner); cascade issues an UPDATE on the existing visit row — no new visits row
No entry point is added to the owner detail page this slice (per prd-entry non-goal)

patterns.description: Owner.getPet(Integer) aggregate-navigation-by-identity; mirror it with a new Pet.getVisit(Integer) returning the live collection member so the edit @ModelAttribute returns the actual Visit instance, not a copy

processNewVisitForm's non-future date check (rejectValue date, typeMismatch.visitDate) plus Visit's @NotBlank description — the edit POST validates identically; controller-held business rule matches the existing feature-package style

risks.risk: The shared @ModelAttribute loadPetWithVisit unconditionally does new Visit() + pet.addVisit(visit); it runs for every mapping in the controller. Left as-is on the edit path it would bind onto a phantom new visit and add a second visits row, breaking 'no second visit added' and 'update in place'.
risks.mitigation: Branch the @ModelAttribute on presence of the {visitId} path variable (e.g. @PathVariable(required=false) Integer visitId): visitId present -> return pet.getVisit(visitId) (the live member); absent -> keep booking behavior. Bind form fields onto that live instance and save the owner — id is preserved (setAllowedFields already disallows id/*.id), so cascade emits UPDATE not INSERT.

risks.risk: Correcting a visit not belonging to the named pet, or a pet not belonging to the named owner, must be refused (acceptance criterion).
risks.mitigation: Extend loadPetWithVisit to throw IllegalArgumentException when pet.getVisit(visitId) is null, mirroring the existing owner-not-found and pet-not-found throws already in that method.

notes: Template: pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm already renders the visit's date and description, so the GET renders prefilled from the model 'visit' automatically; verify the form's action posts back to the current (edit) URL for both flows. Flash-message wording on success is implementer's choice (PRD names no text). Date-check duplication between the new and edit POST is acceptable per the codebase's controller-held-rule style; extracting a private helper is an optional Refactor-step cleanup, not required.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Object-level authorization is enforced by strict aggregate navigation: loadPetWithVisit resolves owner.getPet(petId) then pet.getVisit(visitId), throwing IllegalArgumentException on any mismatch. A visit is unreachable across a pet or owner boundary (including a sibling pet of the same owner), since pet.getVisit only scans that pet's own visit collection — no IDOR/BOLA introduced

Mass-assignment / id tampering is blocked: setAllowedFields disallows id and *.id, so form binding cannot rewrite visit.id to redirect the in-place update; Pet.getVisit also filters !visit.isNew() and matches by identity
Data integrity preserved: the correction binds onto the live collection member and persists via the aggregate root (owners.save), producing an UPDATE rather than a second visit row

No injection surface added: no SQL string-building (Spring Data JPA), path variables are int/Integer, exception messages interpolate only numeric ids, and the description renders through Thymeleaf auto-escaping
No supply-chain change: build files and dependencies untouched, so no new CVE surface

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The @BeforeEach block introduced in this slice constructs Owner, Pet, and Visit with direct new-operator calls (`new Owner()`, `new Pet()`, `new Visit()`). Testing-principles.md §Test Data Construction applies from 2026-07-31: a slice that adds new tests writes them behind factory methods from the start. No factory methods exist for these types yet, so they must be introduced here.
findings.fix: Introduce package-scoped factory helpers (e.g., `createAnOwner()`, `createAPet()`, `createAVisit(LocalDate date, String description)`) and replace the three direct constructor calls in @BeforeEach with calls to those helpers. The helpers should set the minimal state each factory produces, leaving callers to set only the fields that matter to the test.

findings.description: Multiple bare numeric and string literals introduced by this slice are Tier-3 mystery values: `plusDays(3)` (setup date offset), `plusDays(5)` (correction date offset in four new tests), `"rabies shot"` (setup description), and `"booster shot"` (correction description in three new tests). The three-tier naming convention (testing-principles.md §Three-Tier Data Naming) requires every literal to be either named by role (Tier 1) or declared irrelevant with a SOME_/ANY_ prefix (Tier 2). The class-level constant `int unknownVisitId = 99` in `theCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenVisitDoesNotBelongToPet` (line 190) has the same problem: the value 99 is arbitrary and should carry a SOME_ prefix at the variable name.
findings.fix: Declare class-level or method-level constants: e.g. `private static final int EXISTING_VISIT_DAYS_AHEAD = 3;`, `private static final int CORRECTION_DAYS_AHEAD = 5;`, `private static final String SOME_DESCRIPTION = "rabies shot";`, `private static final String CORRECTED_DESCRIPTION = "booster shot";`. Rename the local `unknownVisitId` to `SOME_UNKNOWN_VISIT_ID` (or use a constant). Reference these in all call sites.

findings.description: `theCorrectedVisitShouldBeUpdatedInPlace` asserts that the in-memory `visit` object is mutated and that the response redirects, but does not verify that `owners.save(owner)` was called. The production code's save call at `VisitController.processUpdateVisitForm` could be removed and this test would still pass — the @ModelAttribute binding mutates the live `visit` object before the save, so the post-request state assertions and redirect check are satisfied regardless of whether persistence occurs. This leaves a behavioral gap: a future regression that deletes or bypasses the save line will not be caught.
findings.fix: Add `then(this.owners).should().save(any(Owner.class));` (BDDMockito) after the mockMvc call. The OwnerRepository is already a MockitoBean, so interaction verification is available without introducing new mocking infrastructure.

findings.description: PRD edge case 3 states: 'Correcting a visit that does not belong to the named pet, **or a pet not belonging to the named owner**, is refused rather than applied.' `theCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenVisitDoesNotBelongToPet` covers only the visit-not-in-pet arm. The owner-validation arm (an ownerId that does not match any owner, or a petId that does not belong to that owner) is exercised on the booking path by pre-existing tests but is not confirmed for the edit URL. The shared @ModelAttribute handles both arms, so a regression in the ownership guard on the edit route would not be caught.
findings.fix: Add `theCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenPetDoesNotBelongToOwner` (or a parametrized test) that requests `GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit` with a petId that is not in the owner's pet list and asserts the expected refusal (IllegalArgumentException root cause, matching the owner-not-found/pet-not-found guard already present in loadPetWithVisit).
